title: B190 — Build our own issue-readiness scorer (replace SpecBot)
description:
## Why

SpecBot (adopted in the B119 walk, 2026-09-25) scores a Linear issue's readiness for an AI coding agent and caught a real, systemic gap: [EMA-240](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-240/b182-shared-agent-memory-across-harnesses-claude-code-codex-opencode) scored **51/100** (acceptance criteria 12, edge cases 10, priority/scope 12). It is useful, but it is a third-party cloud judge with a 25-analyses/month free cap, an opaque rubric and scoring model, and nothing the lab can gate CI on. Build a lab-owned equivalent that scores the same way, runs on the lab's own models, and can gate.

## Scope

1. **Reconstruct the rubric from SpecBot's published output** (black-box, from its comments — no decompiling): the 8 dimensions it reports (objective/problem · expected behavior · acceptance criteria · edge cases · technical context · dependencies · reproduction steps · priority & scope clarity), per-dimension 0–100, a weighted total, threshold 80, blockers vs suggested fixes, confidence.
2. **Scorer**: an LLM judge over the issue (title + description + labels + priority + relations), via the lab's model gateway (LiteLLM, agentic lane) — model choice from the lab's judge experience (B84/B100: `qwen2.5:7b` was the reliable local judge). Structured JSON out; deterministic checks first (does an "Acceptance criteria" section with ≥1 checkbox exist?) so the LLM only judges what text can't.
3. **Trigger**: the lab can't receive Linear webhooks (LAN), so: an on-demand CLI (`scripts/issue-readiness.sh EMA-###`) + a scheduled/CI sweep of open issues, posting a comment back to the issue (write key from `scripts/.env`).
4. **Calibration** against SpecBot: score the same issues with both; agree within a tolerance before SpecBot is retired.
5. **Gate** (optional, decided in-flight): fail `check-linear-sync` / CI for open High issues below threshold.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `issue-readiness EMA-240` prints the 8 dimension scores, the total, blockers and suggested fixes, and exits non-zero below 80 (output captured).
- [ ] On ≥10 issues scored by both, the lab scorer's total is within ±10 of SpecBot's on at least 8, and it flags the same blockers on [EMA-240](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-240/b182-shared-agent-memory-across-harnesses-claude-code-codex-opencode)'s pre-fix version.
- [ ] Deterministic checks run before the LLM: an issue with no Acceptance-criteria section is scored ≤20 on that dimension without an LLM call (unit-tested).
- [ ] Posting is idempotent: re-scoring an unchanged issue updates its one comment instead of adding a new one.
- [ ] Model gateway down → the command exits 2 "scorer unavailable", never a score (fail closed; bats test asserts the REASON, not just the status).
- [ ] bats + pytest tests run in the Docker toolchain image and in CI; runbook + demo (DoD).

## Edge cases & failure modes

* Empty or one-line descriptions; very long descriptions (context limits — truncate with a visible note, never silently).
* Bucket issues (children carry the detail) and Stud.IO-project issues (different conventions) — score with the right template or skip explicitly.
* LLM returns malformed JSON or out-of-range scores → rejected and retried once, then exit 2.
* Score drift between model versions → the model + rubric version is recorded in each comment.
* Rate limits on a hosted fallback model → back off; never post a partial score.

## Enforcement comparators (added 2026-09-26, from the B119 walk)

**LineGuard** and **Required** (both Linear integrations; pricing unknown) watch issue changes and, when a rule fails (a required field missing for a workflow state), **move the issue back and comment with what's missing**. That is the gentler, in-Linear form of this item's optional gate — e.g. "can't enter In Progress below 80 / without Acceptance criteria". The lab's scorer can do the same by polling the API (move back + comment) — no webhooks needed. Together: templates shape → B190 scores → the gate enforces, closing B119's original finding that nothing enforces fields.

## Out of scope

* Rewriting issues automatically (the scorer reports; a human or harness edits).
* Scoring projects, initiatives or documents.
* Receiving Linear webhooks (no LAN ingress) — polling/CI only.
* Paid scoring services.

## Reverse-engineering evidence so far ([EMA-240](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-240/b182-shared-agent-memory-across-harnesses-claude-code-codex-opencode), 2026-09-25 — 4 runs)

| Run | Change to the issue | Total | AC | Edge | Tech ctx | Prio/scope |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | original (Why / Goal / Scope) | 51 | 12 | 10 | 44 | 12 |
| 2 | added Acceptance criteria, Edge cases, Out of scope | 70 | 90 | 82 | 44 | 12 |
| 3 | (same, re-run) | 70 | 90 | 82 | 44 | 12 |
| 4 | added Technical context table and a Priority & scope section | 75 | 90 | 82 | 84 | **12** |
| 5 | re-run, no change (2026-09-26) | 75 | 90 | 82 | 84 | **12** |

Other dimensions held steady (objective 82, expected behavior 84, dependencies 82, repro 84). **Open question #1:** priority & scope stayed at exactly 12 through a written priority rationale, ordered scope, minimum slice and time-box — so it likely reads Linear's structured fields (estimate? due date? cycle?) or penalizes size, not the text. **The lab does not use estimates** (team estimation is off by the owner's choice, 2026-09-26), so that hypothesis stays untested — and the lab's own scorer must **not** penalize a missing estimate: priority/scope is judged from the native priority field + the written rationale and scope boundary. Runs 2 and 3 were identical — deterministic scoring is a property to match.

Relates B119 (found in the walk), B182 ([EMA-240](https://linear.app/emangini/issue/EMA-240/b182-shared-agent-memory-across-harnesses-claude-code-codex-opencode) — the first issue scored), B84/B100 (LLM judges).
